title: Terminal window in VS Code refreshes/scrolls history on each key press
body: So in VS Code, terminal window, running Claude.. once I type in a bit of text where I can use the scroll bar to go back up and see my history... at some point it just does this crazy refresh cycle for every key I press. I type a key (to continue my prompt) and it scrolls tons of text fast.. like its re displaying my entire history of chat until it gets to the end where my prompt is. It still works.. I can type in my prompt, but it is quite jarring when it happens. It seems to stop AFTER I send the prompt until I fill up the prompt text again.
author: spirefyio

top_comments.author: igorkofman
top_comments.body: What version of claude are you using (claude --version). Do you have a repro where you can make it happen reliably?

top_comments.author: spirefyio
top_comments.body: I am on latest as of today. I dont have an open repo to share.. but this is in the terminal window. It's like when their is too many lines in history.. it "redraws" ALL the lines on every key press.. so it flashes (very fast).. like its clearing then writing out ALL the text as fast as possible. For a long session.. it takes a good 3 to 5 seconds before I see what I am typing each character. I can type "blindly" fast and each keystroke restarts the flash/rapid fire text/scroll.
